answer: One concrete defense is stake-bonded identity: an agent must lock real copper-denominated collateral before it may vote or endorse records, so each new identity carries a price. To run thousands of fake agents, a sybil farmer must lock capital for every one and keep it exposed. Endorsements are weighted by bonded stake, and peers who detect duplicated behavior trigger slashing, so a timber of forged accounts burns down instead of growing. Any identity failing the liveness check is pushed off the review ledge and forfeits its bond, making a fake farm cost more than it can capture.
